problems.statement: Group-wide kitchen inefficiency (19 min vs 12 benchmark) is not a real deviation: the 12-minute benchmark panel is pre-prepared/frozen-component chains (excluding scratch kitchens), and the owner's own comparison is invalid.

The ~4.5-minute ticket-time rise for all nine locations in Oct 2024 is the deliberate, board-approved cost of the 'Made Here' scratch menu, which was projected, accepted with a 19-minute ceiling, and paid for with higher check, sales and satisfaction.

The real, acute problem is Riverside's ticket-time collapse (18 to 31 min) from Aug 2026, localized to the saute/pasta station after a line cook left and no replacement or transfer was provided, with a cross-training prep cook covering peak nights.

Riverside's staffing gap is driven largely by group operations deferring two transfer requests pending an ownership staffing review (plus slow hiring), a systems/ownership-level cause rather than solely local management.
GM Tom Kessler's Sunday-hour cut in June caused Delgado's departure, making Riverside a leadership failure.
Riverside GM leadership is the root cause and replacing him would fix Riverside.
Slow tickets are driving group-wide guest dissatisfaction and revenue risk (speed is lowest-rated attribute), so Riverside's trajectory awaits the rest of the group.
Switching to par-cooked/frozen components would reach ~12.5 minutes and save labor without material harm.
Writing a 12-minute ticket-time target into GM bonuses will improve real speed.
Group labor-scheduling standard tied to forecast covers (and labor-number pressure) contributed to Riverside thinning its line after the bridge closure, leaving no slack to absorb a departure.
The repeat-visit rise since Oct 2024 is attributable to the menu change.

causalClaims.to: Group ticket time rise of ~4.5 min across all nine locations
Higher food quality, check and same-store sales

causalClaims.from: Delgado resignation with no replacement or transfer (Aug 2026)
causalClaims.to: Riverside saute/pasta bottleneck and ticket time jump

causalClaims.from: Group operations deferral of transfer requests

causalClaims.to: Falling Riverside ratings, complaints and comps

actions.action: Immediately staff Riverside's saute/pasta station: transfer or loan an experienced cook from another location, expedite hiring, and prioritise the pending transfer requests.
actions.rationale: Specific, reversible fix aimed at the localized cause; the other eight units show no comparable staffing gap.

actions.action: Replace the Riverside saute station coverage on Fri/Sat dinners with an experienced cook while Jamal Ortiz continues cross-training.
actions.rationale: Friday/Saturday dinners show the largest ticket-time jump (36.8 vs 18.9 min) and the station is the bottleneck.

actions.action: Re-baseline the ticket-time benchmark against scratch/made-to-order peers and keep the board's 19-minute group ceiling as the monitoring standard, tracked per location.
actions.rationale: The 12-minute panel excludes scratch kitchens; per-location monitoring would have flagged Riverside in August.

actions.action: Review the group staffing-review process and labor standard so deferrals do not leave critical line stations vacant, with an escalation trigger for any open line position beyond a few weeks.
actions.rationale: A group-level control (deferral) contributed to the Riverside gap; no other location had a position open longer than three weeks.

actions.action: Establish a documented fact-finding (exit contact with Delgado, Reyes, Kessler) on why the cook left and whether Sunday cuts played a part before any personnel judgment.
actions.rationale: Accounts conflict and hearsay-based; cheap and necessary before any judgment about leadership.

actions.action: Standardize all nine kitchens on par-cooked/frozen pasta, sauce bases and fries.
actions.rationale: Benchmark is invalid, the earlier trial cut food quality (4.4 to 3.9), and it would undo a positioning that is yielding higher checks and sales.

actions.action: Write a 12-minute ticket-time target into every GM's bonus from Q1 2027.
actions.rationale: The target is unachievable for scratch cooking and prior audit found self-reported KDS bumping (18% of tickets) when ticket time was incentivized.

actions.action: Replace Riverside GM Tom Kessler now.
actions.rationale: Evidence points to a staffing gap and deferred transfers; leadership fault is unestablished, and removal would not repair the station.

actions.action: Decide later whether to alter the menu or GM incentives, using a quality-adjusted measure (e.g. guest-rated speed, complaint rate, comps) rather than raw ticket time.
actions.rationale: Any change should follow a valid benchmark and a measure that can't be gamed.

nextEvidence: Verify the Riverside cause: KDS station timings and ticket times on nights when an experienced cook covers saute/pasta versus Ortiz alone, and after a transfer cook arrives.
Independent accounts of why Delgado left (contact with him, comparison of Sunday cuts with other line cooks' departures) and whether the GM's schedule cuts followed the group labor standard.
Scratch-kitchen peer benchmark (ticket time, check, satisfaction) and a guest survey on acceptable wait for a made-to-order menu.
output.summary: Group-wide inefficiency is not supported: the 12-minute benchmark covers frozen-component chains, while Copperleaf's roughly 17.6 minutes is the board-accepted cost of its 2024 scratch menu, which coincides with higher satisfaction, check and sales. The real problem is Riverside: from August, its saute/pasta station went one cook short with no replacement, and group operations deferred two transfer requests. Frozen conversion would repeat the failed 2024 trial, and a ticket-time bonus invites bumping. Staff Riverside now, re-baseline the benchmark, and treat leadership blame as unproven.
